answer: Wharf-Lottery Assignment. Each agent identity gets a slot in a ferrous-tagged hardware ledger; a public beacon draws a random sequence that assigns tasks and rewards only to slots drawn that epoch. An attacker cannot precompute which clones land paying work, and unused slots decay. A sparrow identifies each ledger entry, so duplicate registrations are detectable at cost. Per-identity cost: hardware plus a forfeited beacon round, making mass cloning economically negative.
